# ---- Load packages from library ----
```{r packages}
packages <- c("tidyverse", "skimr", "gtsummary", "gt",
              "pROC", "janitor", "broom", "here", "parameters",
              "broom.helpers")

lapply(packages, library, character.only = TRUE)
```

```{r load-data}
# ---- Load raw data ----
diabetes_raw <- read_csv(
  here("data", "raw", "pima_diabetes.csv"),
  col_names = FALSE,
  show_col_types = FALSE
)

# ---- Add original column names ----
colnames(diabetes_raw) <- c(
  "Pregnancies", "Glucose", "BloodPressure", "SkinThickness",
  "Insulin", "BMI", "DiabetesPedigreeFunction", "Age", "Outcome"
)

# ---- Recode impossible zeros to NA ----
vars_with_impossible_zeros <- c(
  "Glucose", "BloodPressure", "SkinThickness", "Insulin", "BMI"
)


diabetes_clean <- diabetes_raw %>% 
  mutate(across(all_of(vars_with_impossible_zeros),
  ~ na_if(.x, 0))) %>% 
  drop_na()

# ---- Confirm ----
nrow(diabetes_clean)
ncol(diabetes_clean)

```

```{r explore}
# ---- Structure ----
glimpse(diabetes_clean)

# ---- Descriptive summary ----
skim(diabetes_clean)

# ---- Outcome distribution ----
diabetes_clean %>% count(Outcome) %>% 
  mutate(percent = round(100 * n/sum(n), 1))
```

```{r fit-model}
# ---- Fit logistic regression ----
model <- glm(Outcome ~ BMI + Age + Pregnancies, 
             data = diabetes_clean,
             family = binomial(link = "logit"))

# ---- Model summary ----
summary(model)

# ---- Tidy coefficient table ----
tidy(model, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)
```
```{r regression-table}
# ---- Create a publication-ready table of the odds ratios ----
tbl_regression(model, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.inf = TRUE) %>% bold_labels() %>% 
  add_glance_source_note(include = c("nobs", "AIC"))
```
```{r roc-analysis}
# ---- 1. Get predicted probabilities ----
diabetes_clean$predicted_prob <- predict(model, type = "response")

# ---- 2. Calculate the ROC object ----
roc_obj <- roc(diabetes_clean$Outcome, diabetes_clean$predicted_prob)

# ---- 3. Get the AUC and 95% Confidence Interval ----
auc_value <- auc(roc_obj)
ci_auc <- ci.auc(roc_obj)

print(auc_value)
print(ci_auc)

# ---- 4. Plot the ROC curve ----
ggroc(roc_obj, color = "#C44E52", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 1, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    title = "ROC Curve for Diabetes Prediction Model",
    subtitle = paste0("AUC = ", round(auc_value, 3)),
    x = "Specificity (False Positive Rate)",
    y = "Sensitivity (True Positive Rate)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```
```{r extract-values, include=FALSE}
# Extract odds ratios for the text
or_table <- tidy(model, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)
glucose_or <- round(or_table$estimate[or_table$term == "Glucose"], 2)
glucose_ci_low <- round(or_table$conf.low[or_table$term == "Glucose"], 2)
glucose_ci_high <- round(or_table$conf.high[or_table$term == "Glucose"], 2)

# Extract AUC values for the text
auc_rounded <- round(auc_value, 2)
ci_low <- round(ci_auc[1], 2)
ci_high <- round(ci_auc[3], 2)
```

# ---- Clinical Interpretation ----
The logistic regression model was statistically significant. The strongest predictor of diabetes in this sample was plasma glucose. For every one-unit (mg/dL) increase in fasting glucose, the odds of having diabetes increased by a factor of r glucose_or (95% CI: r glucose_ci_low to r glucose_ci_high), holding other variables constant. BMI, age, and number of pregnancies were also significant positive predictors.

To evaluate the model's discriminatory power, a Receiver Operating Characteristic (ROC) curve was generated. The model achieved an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of r auc_rounded (95% CI: r ci_low to r ci_high).

An AUC of r auc_rounded indicates excellent discrimination. Clinically, this means that if we randomly select one patient with diabetes and one patient without, there is a r auc_rounded * 100% chance that the model will assign a higher risk score to the patient who actually has the disease. The model performed significantly better than random guessing (AUC = 0.5).

```{r save-figure, include=FALSE}
# Ensure the figures directory exists
dir.create(here("figures"), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

# Recreate the plot and save it
roc_plot <- ggroc(roc_obj, color = "#C44E52", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 1, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    title = "ROC Curve for Diabetes Prediction Model",
    subtitle = paste0("AUC = ", round(auc_value, 3)),
    x = "Specificity (False Positive Rate)",
    y = "Sensitivity (True Positive Rate)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

# Save as PNG (300 dpi for journals) and PDF
ggsave(here("figures", "roc_curve.png"), roc_plot, width = 7, height = 6, dpi = 300)
ggsave(here("figures", "roc_curve.pdf"), roc_plot, width = 7, height = 6)
```
